With minor cleanup (e.g., siloxane removal), most biogas is used to generate electricity and heat. To fuel vehicles, biogas must be processed to a higher purity standard. This process is called conditioning or upgrading and involves the removal of water, carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, and other trace elements. The resulting RNG has a higher content of methane than raw biogas, which makes it comparable to conventional natural gas and thus a suitable energy source in applications that require pipeline- quality gas. In general, RNG is sold via book-and-claim in the United States; facilities that are close enough to the end user for a direct connection are far less common. Book-and-claim systems decouple the physical gas from its environmental attributes, allowing the attributes to be verified and transferred via certificates, without the need for the specific gas molecules to reach the buyer. This decoupling allows for greater flexibility in end users and uses and provides RNG producers with much larger markets (RNG Coalition 2023). RNG’s contribution to the economy includes an estimated 55,000 jobs and $7.2 billion to gross domestic product. In 2024, for every 1 TBtu of RNG generated, 314 jobs were created in the United States (Guidehouse 2024). RNG systems offer socioeconomic benefits, including generating revenue streams and boosting local economies. Along with generating revenues from wastes through the sale of renewable energy products, outputs from biogas systems can offer avoided costs of waste management, on-site electricity, heat, and transportation fuel. 2.8.1 Renewable Natural Gas Production and Potential The EPA reports that more than 882 million RINs of compressed RNG, about 82.6 million RINs of liquefied RNG, and about 8.6 million RINs of unspecified RNG were consumed in 2024 (EPA 2025d). One RIN is equal to one ethanol-equivalent gallon and RNG receives D3 celluosic RINs. Figure 33 shows the increase in RNG production over the past 10 years due to a combination of more production facilities coming online and increased production at existing plants. The combined 2024 volume corresponds to about 973 million gallons of ethanol equivalent, or roughly 74.8 TBtu.
